theory.intro: Two triangles are congruent when one fits exactly on the other, even after a flip or a turn. You need not check all six matching parts: each of the four tests below is enough on its own.
steps: List the pairs of sides and angles marked or given as equal.
Check the arrangement: an angle between two given sides is included (SAS); a right angle with the hypotenuse points to RHS.
Match the information to SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS — if no test fits, the triangles are not necessarily congruent.

workedExamples.question_text:
The side lengths of three triangles are listed below. Choose the congruent pair, state the test and write a congruence statement.

$AB=5\text{ cm},\ BC=7\text{ cm},\ AC=8\text{ cm}$.

$DE=5\text{ cm},\ EF=6\text{ cm},\ DF=8\text{ cm}$.

$XY=8\text{ cm},\ YZ=7\text{ cm},\ XZ=5\text{ cm}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$AB=XZ=5\text{ cm}$, $BC=ZY=7\text{ cm}$ and $AC=XY=8\text{ cm}$.

Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal. The matching vertices are $A\leftrightarrow X$, $B\leftrightarrow Z$ and $C\leftrightarrow Y$.

$\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta XZY$ (SSS).

$\Delta DEF$ has a side of $6\text{ cm}$ instead of $7\text{ cm}$.

$AB=DE$ and $AC=DF$.

$\angle BAC=\angle EDF=50^{\circ}$. Each angle lies between the two given sides.

$\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta DEF$ (SAS).

workedExamples.question_text: In $\Delta PQR$, $\angle P=45^{\circ}$, $\angle Q=70^{\circ}$ and $QR=6\text{ cm}$. In $\Delta XYZ$, $\angle X=45^{\circ}$, $\angle Y=70^{\circ}$ and $YZ=6\text{ cm}$. State the congruence test and write a congruence statement.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\angle P=\angle X$ and $\angle Q=\angle Y$.

$QR=YZ=6\text{ cm}$ is a pair of corresponding sides: both sides are opposite the $45^{\circ}$ angle.

$\Delta PQR\equiv\Delta XYZ$ (AAS).

Both triangles are right-angled at $B$ and $Y$.

The hypotenuses satisfy $AC=XZ=15\text{ cm}$, and $BC=YZ=9\text{ cm}$.

$\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta XYZ$ (RHS), with $A\leftrightarrow X$, $B\leftrightarrow Y$ and $C\leftrightarrow Z$.

workedExamples.question_text:
For each pair, give one extra fact that establishes congruence and name the test.

(a) $AB=DE=7\text{ cm}$, $AC=DF=10\text{ cm}$ and $\angle BAC=55^{\circ}$.

(b) $\angle P=\angle X=48^{\circ}$ and $\angle Q=\angle Y=76^{\circ}$ in $\Delta PQR$ and $\Delta XYZ$.

(c) $\Delta KLM$ and $\Delta STU$ are right-angled at $L$ and $T$. Their hypotenuses satisfy $KM=SU=13\text{ cm}$, and $LM=5\text{ cm}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Add $\angle EDF=55^{\circ}$. This is the matching angle between $DE$ and $DF$, so $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta DEF$ (SAS).

(b) Add $QR=YZ$. These sides correspond because $P\leftrightarrow X$, $Q\leftrightarrow Y$ and $R\leftrightarrow Z$. Then $\Delta PQR\equiv\Delta XYZ$ (AAS).

(c) Add $TU=5\text{ cm}$. Both right angles, the hypotenuses and one other pair of corresponding sides match, so $\Delta KLM\equiv\Delta STU$ (RHS).

workedExamples.question_text: $AB=DE=8\text{ cm}$, $AC=11\text{ cm}$, $DF=x\text{ cm}$ and $\angle BAC=\angle EDF=42^{\circ}$. Find $x$ so that $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta DEF$ by SAS.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The $8\text{ cm}$ sides and the included $42^{\circ}$ angles already match. SAS also needs $AC=DF$.

$x=11$.

(a) $AB=CB$ and $\angle ABD=\angle CBD$ (given). $BD=BD$ because it is a common side. The equal angle is included between these sides, so $\Delta ABD\equiv\Delta CBD$ (SAS).

(b) $AB=CB$ and $AD=CD$ (given), and $BD=BD$ (common side). Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, so $\Delta ABD\equiv\Delta CBD$ (SSS).

workedExamples.question_text: In $\Delta ABC$, $\angle A=35^{\circ}$, $\angle B=85^{\circ}$ and $BC=8\text{ cm}$. In $\Delta DEF$, $\angle D=60^{\circ}$, $\angle F=35^{\circ}$ and $DE=8\text{ cm}$. Decide whether the triangles are congruent and give the test.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Using the angle sum of a triangle:

$\begin{align*}\angle C&=180^{\circ}-35^{\circ}-85^{\circ}\\&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\angle E&=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=85^{\circ}\end{align*}$

The matching vertices are $A\leftrightarrow F$, $B\leftrightarrow E$ and $C\leftrightarrow D$. Both $BC$ and $ED$ are opposite the $35^{\circ}$ angle.

$\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta FED$ (AAS).

$\angle BAE=\angle CDE$ and $AE=DE$ (given).

$\angle AEB=\angle DEC$ (vertically opposite angles).

Two pairs of corresponding angles and one pair of corresponding sides are equal, so $\Delta ABE\equiv\Delta DCE$ (AAS).

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Two triangles both have angles $45^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$. Are they necessarily congruent?

(b) Two triangles each have sides of $6\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$ and an angle of $30^{\circ}$ opposite the $6\text{ cm}$ side. Does this establish congruence?

(c) $AB=AC=7\text{ cm}$. Point $D$ lies on $BC$, with $BD=3\text{ cm}$ and $DC=4\text{ cm}$. Are $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta ACD$ congruent?

(d) Two triangles have angles $45^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$. A $10\text{ cm}$ side is opposite $60^{\circ}$ in one and opposite $75^{\circ}$ in the other. Are they congruent?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Equal angles determine shape but allow different sizes. AAA does not establish congruence.

(b) The given angle is not between the two given sides. SSA does not establish congruence; two different triangles can satisfy these givens.

(c) Let $AD=t\text{ cm}$. The side lengths are $7,t,3$ and $7,t,4$. Removing the common lengths leaves $3$ and $4$, so the triangles are not congruent.

(d) The equal $10\text{ cm}$ sides are opposite different angles, so they are not corresponding sides. The triangles are not congruent.

foundation.solution_text:
The tick marks show three pairs of equal corresponding sides.
The triangles are congruent (SSS).

The tick marks show two pairs of equal corresponding sides, and the marked angles between those sides are equal.
Two pairs of sides and the included angle are equal, so the triangles are congruent (SAS).

The single and double arcs show two pairs of equal corresponding angles, and the tick marks show one pair of equal corresponding sides.
The triangles are congruent (AAS).

Both triangles are right-angled, the hypotenuses are marked equal, and one other pair of corresponding sides is marked equal.
The triangles are congruent (RHS).

The side lengths $3$ cm, $5$ cm and $7$ cm match in both triangles.
Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, so the triangles are congruent (SSS).

$4$ cm matches $4$ cm and $6$ cm matches $6$ cm, and the $35^{\circ}$ angle sits between these two sides in each triangle.
Two pairs of sides and the included angle are equal, so the triangles are congruent (SAS).

Both triangles are right-angled.
The hypotenuses are both $11$ m, and another pair of corresponding sides are both $8$ m.
The triangles are congruent (RHS).

The angles $40^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$ match in both triangles, and the $8$ cm sides are corresponding sides.
Two pairs of angles and one pair of corresponding sides are equal, so the triangles are congruent (AAS).

development.question_text:
In $\Delta ABC$, $AB = 8$ cm, $AC = 6$ cm and $\angle BAC = 45^{\circ}$. In $\Delta DEF$, $DE = 8$ cm and $DF = 6$ cm.
State one extra piece of information that would prove $\Delta ABC \equiv \Delta DEF$, and name the congruence test it completes.
development.solution_text:
$AB = DE = 8$ cm and $AC = DF = 6$ cm.
$\angle BAC$ is the angle between the two given sides in $\Delta ABC$, and $\angle EDF$ is the matching included angle in $\Delta DEF$.
$\angle EDF = 45^{\circ}$ would prove $\Delta ABC \equiv \Delta DEF$ (SAS).

Equal angles (AAA) fix the shape of a triangle but not its size.
The second triangle is an enlargement of the first, so the triangles are not congruent.
AAA is not a congruence test, so the triangles are not necessarily congruent.

$\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta GHI$ both have sides $4$, $6$ and $9$; $\Delta DEF$ has a side of $8$ instead of $9$.
Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, matching $A\leftrightarrow G$, $B\leftrightarrow H$ and $C\leftrightarrow I$.
$\Delta ABC \equiv \Delta GHI$ (SSS).

Both triangles are right-angled and the hypotenuses are equal ($PR = XZ = 9$ cm).
One more pair of corresponding sides completes the right-angle test.
$YZ = 4$ cm would prove $\Delta PQR \equiv \Delta XYZ$ (RHS).

The $5$ cm sides match and the $40^{\circ}$ included angles match.
For SAS, the second pair of sides forming the included angle must also be equal.
$x = 7$ cm makes the triangles congruent (SAS).

$AB = CB$ (marked) and $\angle ABD = \angle CBD$ (marked).
$BD$ is a common side, so $BD = BD$.
Two pairs of sides and the included angle are equal: $\Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CBD$ (SAS).

$CA = CB$ (marked) and $AM = BM$ ($M$ is the midpoint of $AB$).
$CM$ is a common side, so $CM = CM$.
Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal: $\Delta ACM \equiv \Delta BCM$ (SSS).

mastery.solution_text:
Left triangle: third angle $= 180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 80^{\circ}$.
Right triangle: third angle $= 180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} - 80^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.
Both triangles have angles $40^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $80^{\circ}$, but the $7$ cm side is opposite the $80^{\circ}$ angle in the first triangle and opposite the $60^{\circ}$ angle in the second.
The equal sides are not corresponding sides, so the triangles are not congruent.

$\angle BAE = \angle CDE$ (marked) and $AE = DE$ (marked).
$\angle AEB = \angle DEC$ (vertically opposite angles).
Two pairs of angles and one pair of corresponding sides are equal: $\Delta ABE \equiv \Delta DCE$ (AAS).

Let $AD = t$ cm.
The side lengths of $\Delta ABD$ are $6$, $t$ and $4$ cm; the side lengths of $\Delta ACD$ are $6$, $t$ and $5$ cm.
These collections of side lengths cannot match in any order: removing the common lengths $6$ and $t$ leaves $4$ and $5$, which are unequal.
Congruent triangles must have the same three side lengths, so $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta ACD$ are not congruent.
